analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Markets were subdued over the prior 24 hours. The S&P 500 closed at 7805 (-0.02%) and the STOXX 600 at 635 (-0.10%). Drivers were an AI-related chip selloff, weak US bank stocks at the start of earnings season, and persistent inflation fears.

US September CPI is due today and DB economists expect a strong headline. They forecast motor fuel +9.6% m/m, headline CPI +0.57% m/m (consensus +0.60%, prior +0.40%), the strongest month since April, shortly after the Iran conflict began. They see the y/y rate rising to +3.6%, the highest since May.

DB expects core CPI to be softer at +0.16% m/m (consensus +0.20%, prior +0.30%), leaving core y/y at +2.4%. The report says surprises either way will shape the narrative into the next Fed meeting, which is two weeks away. PCE data does not arrive until the day after that decision.

Market pricing for an October Fed hike was back up to 24% on Oct 13, the highest since October 1. An underwhelming jobs report and the initial French stress had raised doubts about back-to-back hikes. Elevated oil keeps the speculation alive.

NY Fed President Williams reiterated support for another 25bp hike this year and said he sees no reason at this time to believe more would be needed. This is in line with the September dot plot median. Richmond Fed President Barkin said the Fed needs to grow more restrictive because shocks are continuing and inflation is enduring.

Front-end yields rose globally while the long end fell on risk-off. The US 2yr rose 2.1bps to 4.78% and the UK 2yr rose 1.7bps, with 2yr Bunds unchanged. The US 10yr fell 2.9bps to 5.21% and the 10yr Bund fell 0.8bps to 3.47%.

French 10yr yield fell 5.8bps to 4.84%. The Franco-German 10yr spread stands at 137bps, still clearly above its level before the stress began a couple of weeks ago. Another section of the report cites a 4.9bp tightening.

The Philly semiconductor index (-0.23%) posted a 5th consecutive decline, the first such streak since July. Semiconductors and semiconductor equipment make up over a sixth of the S&P 500, so the sector can drive the overall index.

Data center stocks lagged: CoreWeave -3.05%, Applied Digital -3.48%, GDS Holding -2.60%. CoreWeave is a large high-yield issuer this year, and its 5Y CDS closed 79bps wider after briefly trading above 1000bps intraday.

US bank earnings started with weakness. JPMorgan (-0.86%) reported an unexpected decline in fixed-income trading revenue and all 24 other KBW Banks Index members also closed lower. The index fell -1.39%. Goldman Sachs (-0.23%) missed on fixed income but beat on equity trading. Citi (-5.60%) was the worst performer despite a fixed-income revenue beat.

Energy prices rose again. European front-month natural gas (+3.40%) hit a post-2022 high of €87.22/MWh. Brent crude fell -0.90% to $105.69/bbl, but the 12-month Brent future (+1.12%) hit a 2026 high of $87.37/bbl, the highest since August 2022. The 1yr Euro inflation swap rose 7.3bps to 3.59%.

Asian equities are mostly higher as chip stocks rebound, with oil capping gains. KOSPI +1.13%, Nikkei +0.89%, Hang Seng +0.16%, ASX 200 -0.66%, CSI 300 -0.31%, Shanghai Composite +0.01%. S&P 500 futures +0.22%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.24%, Stoxx futures +0.34%.

China September CPI was +0.9% y/y versus +1.0% expected and +0.8% in August. PPI rose +5.0% y/y versus +4.4% expected and +3.8% in August, the highest since June 2022. The report attributes this to resilient business demand, AI-related input costs and Middle East supply disruptions.
China September trade beat expectations. Exports rose +36.3% y/y versus +25.7% expected, the strongest since February. Imports rose +31.0% versus +25.0% expected, the fastest since June.
US data was light. NFIB small business optimism fell to 97.9 versus 98.2 expected. September existing home sales were 3.99m annualised versus 3.95m expected.

Today's calendar includes the Fed Beige Book, speeches from ECB's Lagarde, Elderson, Pereira, Escriva, Makhlouf and Schnabel, and the Fed's Bowman and Barkin. Bank of America, Morgan Stanley and BlackRock report earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: elevated oil and a strong CPI could support hike pricing. Williams backs one more 25bp hike and Barkin says inflation is enduring and the Fed should be more restrictive.
tension_points.bear_case: Doubts remain on whether the Fed can deliver back-to-back hikes after the underwhelming jobs report. DB expects core CPI to be soft at +0.16% m/m, and Williams sees no reason to do more than one more hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A CPI surprise in either direction would shape the narrative into the Fed meeting two weeks away.
